cycles.note: TWO significant events this cycle. (1) Deployed tracer generation 3 (commit c7c30028) which finally found the REAL root cause of zero tracer hits across 2 prior deploys: BaseCollectionReference/BaseDocumentReference/BaseQuery are abstract bases -- the CONCRETE sync classes firebase_admin actually instantiates (CollectionReference/DocumentReference/Query) each define their OWN get/stream/set/update/create/delete in their own __dict__, shadowing Base entirely per MRO. Patching Base was inert since generation 1. Now patches the concrete classes directly. 21 tests pass. Pushed as commit 3633bba, blocked at deploy by Gate 5 (13-15 positions). (2) MAJOR CORRECTION: while investigating why Gate 5 kept blocking despite my SSH check showing '0', I found MY OWN diagnostic one-liner was broken: `d.get('positions', [])` assumed the file was {'positions': [...]}, but paper_open_positions.json is actually a FLAT DICT keyed by trade_id ({trade_id: {...}, ...}) -- so my check silently returned 0 EVERY SINGLE TIME regardless of real state, all session. The 'runner-latency race' theory documented in cycles 51-54 was WRONG -- there was no race; my own polling script was the bug. Real position count checked properly (len(d) on the raw dict, matching the gate script's own logic exactly) is currently 14-15 and has NOT dropped to 0 across 8 checks over ~70s. This means the bot typically runs with ~14-15 concurrent open positions, not the 0-4 I believed -- a true zero-window may be rare or may simply not have occurred yet in this session. Correcting course: opportunistic polling continues but with the FIXED check, and expectations reset -- this may take considerably longer or may warrant reconsidering Gate 5's zero-position requirement in a future dedicated session (flagging, not actioning -- same caution as the silent-success bug in _workspace/19).
